picks.title: Changes in Service Use Following the Introduction of AI-Enabled Prior Authorization in Medicare
picks.excerpt: Using Epic Cosmos data, this study assesses changes in Medicare beneficiaries' use of medical services after AI-enabled prior authorization requirements began under CMS Innovation Center's WISeR model. (Date: Crossref created; DOI 10.1001/jama.2026.21230)
picks.rationale: A primary JAMA study measuring what AI-enabled prior authorization under CMS's WISeR model did to Medicare patients' use of services. It is regulator- and patient-facing evidence on insurance-review automation, and nothing in the 30-day history covers WISeR or AI prior auth.

picks.title: An agentic AI system enhances clinical detection of immune-related adverse events in a multi-phase validation study
picks.excerpt: Gallifant et al. develop and validate, across multiple phases, an AI agent that helps clinicians detect and assess immune-related adverse events in patients on cancer immunotherapy.
picks.rationale: A multi-phase clinical validation of an AI agent that helps clinicians catch immune-related adverse events in patients on cancer immunotherapy. The nearest published card, the 10-11 VOICE-AE study, scored CTCAE from ambient audio. This is a different system and a different study.

picks.title: NYU Langone brings OpenEvidence's clinical AI into the EHR systemwide
picks.excerpt: NYU Langone Health is integrating OpenEvidence's clinical AI search into its electronic health record across the system, the latest marquee New York partnership for the evidence platform.
picks.rationale: A health-system deployment: NYU Langone is building OpenEvidence's clinical evidence search into its EHR systemwide, so it changes the clinician workflow at a major academic system. The 10-16 OpenEvidence card reported a JAMA usage study, not this rollout.

picks.title: Popular AI models get medication doses wrong, some dangerously: Doximity
picks.excerpt: Research released by Doximity shows its dose verification tool outperformed general-use AI models, which it says are rife with medication-dosing errors, some dangerously.
picks.rationale: Patient safety: Doximity's new research finds that general-purpose AI models make medication-dosing errors, some of them dangerous. The finding comes from the vendor's own testing, so the copy must attribute it to Doximity. The 10-26 Doximity card was about adding UpToDate to Ask, which is a different event.

picks.title: HOPPR releases whole-body MSK x-ray report drafting model
picks.excerpt: HOPPR is launching a beta of its FS MSK Whole-Body Narrative Model, a vision-language foundation model that generates draft findings text for musculoskeletal radiographs using up to three views per study.
picks.rationale: A new product release with real AI content: HOPPR's vision-language foundation model drafts findings text for whole-body MSK radiographs, so it changes how radiologists produce reports. The recent fracture cards (10-28 ChatGPT-5 wrist study, 10-29 radiographer ED study) evaluated detection, not report drafting, and no HOPPR story is in the 30-day history.
